name: Per Ola Kristensson
why: Cambridge Intelligent Interactive Systems Group lead; co-author of Unbounded and Objestures and many mixed-reality text-entry and interaction papers.

name: Fengyuan Zhu
why: University of Toronto DGP researcher working on phones and touch inside VR/MR; first author of Touching The Droid.

name: Ramesh Raskar
why: MIT Media Lab (Camera Culture) professor and projector-AR pioneer (Shader Lamps, iLamps, RFIG Lamps with Johnny Lee); RFIG video exists at youtube.com/watch?v=MURwa1lWDsY.

name: Karen X Cheng
why: Director and creative technologist known for viral camera, AR and AI video tricks; co-made the Spectacles 3 butterfly film with Clara Bacou.

name: PHORIA (Ben Ferns)
why: Melbourne XR studio that co-built the WebXR mixed-reality showcase Spatial Fusion with Lusion and Meta; Ben Ferns posts WebXR tech walkthroughs.

name: Yi-Wen Lin
why: London-based Taiwanese creative coder (WENSDAY) who co-made the AR Virtual Plants demo with Matt DesLauriers; WebGL/AR sketches.

name: Hamill Industries (Pablo Barquín & Anna Diaz)
why: Barcelona visual studio mixing robotics, real-time graphics and computer vision; built the AI dance ensemble Engendered Otherness and CORTEX's live scenography with Kianí del Valle, plus robot-camera live shows for Floating Points.

name: Alberto Novello (JesterN)
why: Sound artist and EEG hacker who wrote the brainwave-to-laser system of (UN)FOCUSSED and made the brain-controlled performance Fragmentation.

name: Andrej Boleslavský (id144)
why: Interactive artist and Mária Júdová's long-time collaborator on Camouflage, body(input); and Everywhen; also made interactive particle installations such as Flow at Signal Festival.

name: Yago de Quay
why: Musician-dancer who performs with Kinect-tracked movement driving music and visuals (Dance Jockey, Breakdown with visiophone).

name: Choy Ka Fai
why: Singapore-born Berlin artist working on dance, motion capture and trance; co-directed the VR piece Constellation of the Flesh with Mária Júdová.

name: The Sancho Plan (Ed Cookson)
why: Bristol audiovisual group behind Big Screen Augmented Reality (2010) and live AR music performances with animated characters; only the big-screen piece was added here (under Neil Mendoza).

name: Oriol Ferrer Mesià
why: openFrameworks developer (ex-Snibbe Interactive) whose Benetton window installations include camera mirrors such as Elastic Mirror, TimeLoop and Kaleidoscope.

name: Tangible Interaction
why: Vancouver studio behind the openFrameworks Digital Graffiti Wall (2010 Olympics) and early marker AR such as AR Hippo for TELUS; mostly commercial, needs a careful pick.

name: Parag K. Mital
why: Artist-researcher whose 'Memory' (2010, with Agelos Papadakis) augments hanging glass sculptures with projected faces; also real-time audiovisual resynthesis mirrors.

name: Champagne Valentine (with Aaron Meyers)
why: Amsterdam studio that made early webcam AR musical instruments (2010) and interactive shop-window mirrors with openFrameworks developer Aaron Meyers.

name: Patrick Baudisch
why: HPI Potsdam professor behind Imaginary Reality Gaming, Imaginary Phone and many body-scale interaction prototypes (Holz's PhD advisor).

name: Andreas Fender
why: First author of Causality-preserving Asynchronous Reality and InfinitePaint (ETH Zurich); mixed-reality work on time and physical causality.

name: Lung-Pan Cheng
why: Lead author of Reality Rifts; known for TurkDeck and Haptic Turk (people as haptic props for VR); National Taiwan University.

name: Mohamed Kari
why: First author of TransforMR and SoundsRide (Porsche / ETH Zurich); mixed reality that re-skins the street and the car ride.

name: Philip Schuette
why: Dutch artist behind playful interactive installations SUN (a bouncy ball moves the sun) and BODY (your pose as an image search) with Random Studio.

name: Nick Verstand
why: Dutch audiovisual artist, co-creator of ANIMA with onformative; makes light-and-sound installations that respond to visitors.

name: Matt Clugston
why: Creative director and motion-graphics artist behind the real-time mocap imagery in Holosphere's Waterhall performance and the University of Birmingham projection show.

name: Job van Nuenen
why: Built the interactive framework and sound for Children of the Light's ZEROTIME, where visitors' phone torches are turned into a live soundscape.

name: Stuart Batchelor
why: Computer artist who co-created the participatory shemza.digital painting apps and installations with Aphra Shemza.

name: Pe Lang
why: Swiss kinetic artist and Zimoun's collaborator; precise magnetic and motor-driven minimal kinetic works with gallery videos (bitforms).

name: Lyman Whitaker
why: American wind sculptor ('Whitaker Wind Sculptures'), large outdoor fields of spinning copper forms; strong land-plus-kinetic reference.

name: Tim Prentice
why: Kinetic wind-wall pioneer whose façades of small hanging panels predate Ned Kahn's; few own videos, needs a search.

name: Bob Potts
why: Kinetic sculptor of slow rowing/flying mechanical forms (e.g. 'Ascension'); gallery videos exist.

name: mischer'traxler
why: Vienna design duo; Ephemerā and Curiosity Cloud are responsive kinetic installations where objects react to visitors.

name: Yunchul Kim
why: Korean artist of fluid and kinetic sculptures (Chroma III, Argos); strong kinetic material.

name: Balint Bolygo
why: Makes pendulum and drawing machines that trace motion (trace category).

name: Johannes Langkamp
why: Dutch artist of kinetic light and camera installations (The Movement of Space).

name: Marcelo Coelho & Jamie Zigelbaum
why: Six-Forty by Four-Eighty (2011): physical light 'pixels' you pick up and rearrange on a wall, which pass colours through touch — a tangible responsive display.

name: Heinz Mack
why: ZERO co-founder with Piene; Light Dynamo (1963) and light rotors are motorised light kinetics (artdone UDKw6xcHiS0, museumabteiberg kNEKdpXI2WQ).

name: Janne Parviainen
why: Finnish light-painting artist who draws glowing figures and 'light bodies' in real rooms and landscapes; strong trace-category candidate, videos on YouTube (e.g. Cambridge Creation Lab talk).

name: Jason D. Page
why: Light-painting artist and founder of LightPaintingPhotography.com; documentary available, could extend the light-painting cluster.

name: Nils-Udo
why: German pioneer of nature art (nests, leaf rafts, flower paintings in landscape); only weak third-party videos found.

name: Susumu Shingu
why: Japanese wind sculptor (Wind Caravan, Wind Museum); makes wind visible in landscapes; only short fan clips found.

name: Heather Hansen
why: Emptied Gestures: charcoal drawings made by her whole body's motion; own YouTube channel exists (C4oBc-o1npg), a trace/performance piece rather than landscape.

name: James Brunt
why: UK land artist making large stone and leaf mandalas in parks; several videos (e.g. EBdxm2DOKFs).

name: Julien Berthier
why: French artist of the half-sunk boat Love Love and a rock-camouflaged boat; illusion in landscape.

name: Jeppe Hein
why: Modified Social Benches and mirror labyrinths in parks; possible overlap with an illusion batch.

name: Spencer Tunick
why: Mass nude installations in landscapes and cities; relevant as bodies placed in place but sensitive content, skipped.

name: Michael Grab (Gravity Glue)
why: Stone balancing in rivers; collaborator of Richard Shilling; own YouTube channel.

name: Martin Hill and Philippa Jones
why: New Zealand ephemeral land art made from ice, leaves and stone, photographed in wilderness.

name: Mark Dion
why: Ecological installations and follies in parks (Neukom Vivarium); nature as museum.

name: Pinar Yoldas / Superflex (One Two Three Swing!)
why: Public installations turning parks into play; Superflex's giant swings along the landscape.

name: Digital Domain / AV Concepts — Tupac hologram (Coachella 2012)
why: The most famous Pepper's-ghost stage 'hologram'; Snoop Dogg's channel has the performance (TGbrFmPBV0Y).

name: ABBA Voyage (ILM / Industrial Light & Magic)
why: Virtual concert with 'ABBAtars' on a purpose-built stage in London, 2022 — current state of holographic theatre.

name: Yiyun Kang
why: Korean artist who projection-maps video onto sculptures and museum spaces (Casting at the V&A, Origin for Jaeger-LeCoultre).

name: William Kentridge / The Centre for the Less Good Idea — The Pepper's Ghost
why: Kentridge's Pepper's-ghost theatre boxes and performances; relevant to holographic theatre if not covered by another batch.

name: Clément Briend
why: French artist projecting faces and religious figures onto trees (3D tree projections), close to Craig Walsh.

name: Pixel Artworks
why: UK projection and immersive studio (daylight-visible projection for Fabergé at Harrods); possibly what 'Projection Artworks' refers to.

name: Kurt Hentschläger
why: ZEE (2008): a fog-filled room lit by stroboscopic light that produces hallucinated patterns; immersive perception piece.

name: Iván Navarro
why: Neon and mirror 'infinity' holes and ladders in floors and walls; illusion of endless depth.

name: Josiah McElheny
why: Mirrored glass boxes such as An End to Modernity and Island Universe reflections; infinite regress illusions.

name: Lucas Samaras
why: Mirrored Room (1966): a room entirely clad in mirrors, a precursor of Kusama's rooms; museum footage needed.

name: Anila Quayyum Agha
why: Intersections: a single lantern casting intricate Islamic-pattern shadows over a whole room; light & illusion.

name: Spencer Finch
why: Recreates specific skies and daylight (e.g. the light of Monet's pond) with filters and fluorescents.

name: Mary Corse
why: Light-and-space painter; glass-microsphere paintings that change with the viewer's position.

name: Meow Wolf
why: House of Eternal Return and later sites: narrative immersive environments; only fan walkthrough videos found in this pass.

name: Carsten Nicolai (alva noto)
why: Light/sound installations such as unicolor and α (alpha) pulse; kin of Ryoji Ikeda.

name: Marek Simonik (Record3D)
why: Record3D app author; open Unity VFX Graph demos stream iPhone LiDAR/TrueDepth point clouds live into VFX Graph (no own demo video found).

name: Dan Miller
why: Unity AR evangelist; open ARFoundation_VFX and ARBodyTrackingVFX repos (AR Foundation + VFX Graph); videos likely on X @DanMillerDev.

name: Saki Komikado (komietty)
why: Geometry programmer; open Unity moxi ink painting, CIP fluid, bitonic-sort SPH and vector-field repos; videos likely on X.

name: Masatatsu Nakamura (mattatz)
why: Open Unity CellularGrowth, Dendrite, voxelizer, procedural tree/flower and volume rendering repos; demo videos mostly GIF/X.

name: Cyanilux
why: Shader Graph artist with open URP repos (retro CRT, watercolour, custom lighting); showcase videos on X.

name: Roel Kok
why: Kinect-VFX-Graph (213 stars): Kinect depth feed into Unity VFX Graph; needs a playable video.

name: Codrin-Mihail (Kodrin)
why: Open VFX-Essentials HDRP workshop and GPU-FlowField compute-shader particle repos.

name: Angela He (zephyo)
why: 2D-Unity-Experiments (279 stars): URP/Shader Graph visual experiments; videos likely on X @zephybite.

name: Ronald van Wijnen
why: Author of spectral.js, an open-source Kubelka-Munk pigment color-mixing library with web demos; Keijiro ported it to Unity for Fluo and his pigment fluid-art tests.

name: FMS_Cat (0b5vr)
why: Demoscene and WebGL real-time visuals artist who performed alongside Keijiro at Channel and Liquidroom; publishes source code.

name: AMAGI (fand)
why: Web graphics artist behind vfx-js and VEDA live-coding tools; active in the same Tokyo live-coding scene.

name: kaiware007
why: Unity VJ shader developer (reaction-diffusion, hex tiling, VJ shader talks) with public repos.

name: Koki Ibukuro (asus4)
why: Unity AR developer (ARKitStreamer, ARFoundationReplay, tf-lite-unity-sample); WorldEnsemble plays music in the geospatial AR world, with source.

name: Jason Tsorlinis
why: BoidsUnity: GPU boids in Unity compute shaders (~100 stars), shown on X with video.

name: MatrixRex
why: Uber-Stylized-Water, a 500-star open stylized water shader for Unity 6 with many water types.

name: Tooster (T3sT3ro)
why: SdfManipulator: interactive real-time SDF editor in Unity that generates raymarching shaders.

name: TLabAltoh
why: Unity-SDF-UI-Toolkit: SDF-based UI shapes and effects for Unity, with X demo videos.

name: Robin Seibold
why: Unity-URP-CelShadeLit: open multi-light cel shader for URP (~150 stars) with X video.

name: Olivier Goguel
why: realtimehand: real-time hand tracking package for Unity (~260 stars), shown on X.

name: Codrin Mihail (Kodrin)
why: HDRP-VFXGraph-Workshop: open VFX Graph workshop project with X demo videos.
